newsitem.title: USA: Maine homosexual rights bill signed.
newsitem.headline: Maine homosexual rights bill signed.

text.p: Gov. Angus King signed into law a gay rights bill Friday, ending 20 years of legislative frustration for activists who now face a repeal effort.
"We have enemies in Maine. They are poverty, disease, ignorance. They are not gay people," King told a ceremony attended by lawmakers who sponsored earlier unsucessful gay rights measures.

The law banned discrimination in housing, credit, public accommodations and employment based on sexual preference in Maine. A similar measure was headed to the desk of neighbourhing New Hampshire Gov. Jeanne Shaheen. Shaheen promised to sign the bill.
Gay rights activists in Maine pushed for anti-discrimination legislation in the state for the past two decades. The Legislature approved a measure in 1994, but it was vetoed by Gov. John Mckernan.

The Christian Civic League of Maine filed papers to hold a vote to overturn the law. The group could force a November referendum by collecting 52,000 signatures in the 90 days after the Legislature adjourns in June.
Maine voters in 1995 solidly defeated a referendum that would have barred local communities from adopting gay rights ordinances.
Political observers said the Catholic Church's position will be critical in any referendum. The church opposed the 1995 referendum but has not said if it will support the bill signed Friday.
